{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the draft MSA against the playbook and identified **18 findings: 8 compliant, 7 deviations and 3 missing clauses**. The risk allocation is unusually mixed: the Vendor-facing protections we care most about are already strong, while the Customer-facing restrictions are aggressive and, in several places, internally contradictory.

What is already acceptable and needs no redline: limitation of liability (§21 — mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with a full carve-out set), assignment and change of control (§24 — unrestricted Customer assignment, Vendor bound asymmetrically in our favour), audit rights (§22), auto-renewal and the 30-day opt-out with a CPI/3% uplift cap (§8), warranties and remedies (§19), licence grant scope (§13), Vendor insurance (§18), and the absence of any Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.

The problems cluster in two places. First, a set of one-sided restrictions on us — a three-year USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" (§2.1), a disclose-and-match obligation that operates as both de facto exclusivity and an MFN against us (§7.2), a 24-month all-territory non-compete and an outright 24-month no-hire (both numbered §12.4) — each of which is contradicted by §12.3, where the Vendor expressly acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. Second, structural gaps: **there is no indemnification article at all** (the outline runs from §19 to §21, while §§9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 each assume one exists, and §9.3 cross-references a non-existent "Section 20.5"), no termination-for-convenience right for Customer in a three-year committed term, and no transition-assistance or data-return/deletion obligation. Governing law is also internally inconsistent: §28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts while §28.2 vests exclusive jurisdiction in New York County, New York.

Drafting note: proposed redlines have been generated and verified for all items below except **GOVLAW (§28.1/28.2)** and **NOSOLICIT (§12.4)**, where the automated edit did not pass verification. Those two require manual drafting before we send comments.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | §21.1 (with §§1.5, 21.2–21.4, 18.2) | Meets preferred position; no redline. |
| 2 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §24.1 (with §§24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Meets preferred position in full; Vendor bound asymmetrically in our favour. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 (first clause so numbered) | De facto exclusivity/ROFR; fails fallback. Redline verified. |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | §27.3 (with §§7.3, 24.4, 8–10) | No Customer-payable LDs or penalties; take-or-pay handled under MINCOMMIT. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | §13.1 (with §§13.2–13.3, 14.3, 10.1) | Meets preferred position; §14.2 language addressed under IP. |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 (duplicate-numbered) | 24 months, any product, any territory, no carve-outs. Redline verified. |
| 7 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §22.1 (with §§22.2–22.3) | Matches preferred position on all material terms. |
| 8 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 | Open-ended obligation to extend Vendor better third-party terms. Redline verified. |
| 9 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitment | **Deviation** | §2.1 | USD 2m/year for three years, take-or-pay, no reduction or exit. Redline verified. |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §8.2 (with §8.3) | Preferred position; missed-reminder extension runs in our favour. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | §19.1 (with §§19.2–19.5, 6.2) | Meets or exceeds preferred position; disclaimer is mutual and carved back. |
| 12 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | §28.1 (conflicts with §28.2) | Singapore law/exclusive Singapore courts; outside accepted set. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |
| 13 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | No §20; see §19.5 and cross-refs at §§9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5 | No indemnity article at all; §9.3 cross-reference is broken. Insertion drafted and verified. |
| 14 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §18.1 (with §18.2) | Meets preferred position; cyber/privacy at USD 5m. |
| 15 | Low | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | §14.2 (with §§14.1, 14.3, 14.4) | Vendor owns all Deliverables; Customer gets revocable term licence. Fails preferred and fallback. Redline verified. |
| 16 | Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 | One-way outright no-hire, all employees, 24 months, no carve-outs. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |
| 17 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | §9 (only §§9.1–9.3, 9.5; no §9.4) | No Customer convenience right in a three-year committed term. Insertion drafted and verified. |
| 18 | Low | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | §10.1 (with §16.5) | No transition duty; no data return or certified deletion; §16.5 defers to a non-existent §11. Insertion drafted and verified. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be presented to the Vendor as conditions of signature, not as negotiating preferences:

1. **§2.1 — take-or-pay minimum commitment.** USD 2,000,000 per year for three years, expressly "without reduction or termination rights," with no termination-for-convenience right elsewhere in the Agreement. Our position: no minimum quantity; Services payable on a usage or ordered basis.
2. **§7.2 — disclose-and-match obligation.** Operates simultaneously as exclusivity/right of first refusal (EXCLUSIVITY) and as an MFN against us (MFN): unlimited as to product, term and comparison methodology, with no exit for Vendor service or delivery failures. Our position: no disclosure or match obligation on Customer.
3. **§12.4 — non-compete.** 24 months post-term, any competing product or service, any territory, no carve-outs. Our position: no non-compete and no field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer.
4. **Missing indemnification article (§20).** No Vendor IP indemnity at all, and §9.3 cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5," which does not exist. Our position: insert §20 at the preferred level, including the §20.5 infringement remedies so the §9.3 cross-reference resolves.
5. **No Customer termination for convenience (§9).** Absence of any convenience right in a three-year term carrying a USD 2m annual commitment. Our position: new §9.4 — 30 days' written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.
6. **§28.1 — governing law and venue.** Singapore law with exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is outside the accepted set (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and conflicts with §28.2's exclusive New York County jurisdiction.

Note for the business: items 1–3 are each directly contradicted by **§12.3**, in which the Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. That internal inconsistency is our strongest lever and we should lead with it.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Confirm the commercial mandate on §2.1** with the business owner before we send comments — whether we can accept any committed volume, and if so at what level and with what reduction mechanic. The rest of the package is legal-led; this one is not.
2. **Manually draft the two failed redlines** before circulation: (a) §28.1/28.2 — conform governing law to New York, delete the conflicting Singapore forum wording, and confine the §28.2 injunctive-relief carve-out to the New York County courts so that law and forum form one permitted pair; (b) §12.4 — narrow to a mutual 12-month non-solicit of personnel directly involved in the Services, striking the no-hire words and the "regardless of how the employee applies" sweep-up, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
3. **Raise the duplicate numbering and broken cross-references** as a clean-up point in the same round: two clauses numbered §7.2 and two numbered §12.4; the outline jumps from §19 to §21; §9.3 cites a non-existent §20.5; §16.5 defers to a non-existent §11; §23 has no operative text; and there is no §9.4. We should ask the Vendor to reissue a renumbered draft so our comments map cleanly.
4. **Send the verified redlines** for §§2.1, 7.2, 12.4 (non-compete), 14.2, and the three insertions (§9.4, §20, §10.3), each with a short \[Playbook\] comment stating the position and, where sensible, the fallback.
5. **Do not reopen** the compliant items (§§8, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24, 27.3). They meet or exceed our preferred positions and there is no benefit to us in putting them back in play.
6. **Escalate** if the Vendor refuses on the walk-away items, particularly the missing indemnity and the take-or-pay/no-exit combination, which together leave us paying USD 6m over three years with no exit and no recourse for third-party IP claims."}
